memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord will send on you curses, confusion and rebuke in everything you put your hand to, until you are destroyed and come to sudden ruin because of the evil you have done in forsaking him... The Lord will plague you with diseases until he has destroyed you from the land you are entering to possess." — Deut 28:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God names the root of the coming ruin plainly: "because of the evil you have done in forsaking him." At the heart of every curse in this chapter is one central sin — forsaking God. Not merely breaking a rule here or there, but abandoning the Lord Himself. When a people turn away from the source of all life and blessing, confusion and ruin naturally follow.

This is worth pausing on. The deepest tragedy is never the loss of crops or comfort; it is the forsaking of God. To turn from Him is to turn from life itself. Like a branch cut off from the vine, we cannot flourish apart from Him (John 15:5-6).

We may not face these specific covenant curses, but the warning against forsaking God speaks to every heart. There is a quiet, gradual kind of drifting that leads a person away from the Lord without a single dramatic decision. Little by little, prayer fades, Scripture is neglected, other loves take over, and the soul grows cold.

The remedy is to keep returning to God, to keep our hearts anchored in Him. And the great comfort of the gospel is this: even when we wander, God does not forsake His own. He holds us fast in Christ, who promised never to leave us (Heb 13:5). Stay close to the One who is your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I in any danger of quietly drifting away from God?
2. What would it look like to keep my heart anchored in Him this season?
3. How does Christ's promise never to leave me steady my soul?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from drifting away from You. Anchor my heart in Your love, and thank You that in Christ You will never forsake me. Hold me close. Amen.
